45.0.s.en: (1) The power and glory of the King

45.0.0.en: 1- My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.

45.0.1.en: 1- David speaks a good word, which comes not only from his thought but from his feelings, that is, from his heart. By the work of the Holy Spirit in his heart he uttered these great and good words. He is speaking to the King, that is, the King of kings, God, and not an earthly king; he certainly does not mean himself. And he says that his tongue is like the heart of a ready writer, that is, that the Holy Spirit overflowing in his heart moves his tongue, so that he writes and utters these words. He senses that the Holy Spirit has turned his heart into a rich spring, overflowing with these words about God.

45.0.2.en: 2- This psalm speaks to us about Christ, God incarnate. God the Father overflowed with His Word, who is the incarnate Christ. This is evident from the description of Christ's attributes in the following verses.

45.0.3.en: 3- David, by the spirit of prophecy, saw Christ and was amazed by Him, and began to speak by the Holy Spirit, as far as he was able, with the expressions we shall see in the following verses. He could not express everything, but only as much as he was able.

45.1.0.en: 2- Thou art fairer than the children of men: grace is poured into thy lips: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.

45.1.1.en: 1- David saw that Christ is fairer than all men. Although He became incarnate and became man like the rest of mankind, His beauty and perfection surpass all, not of course in the form of the body but in righteousness and holiness. His words were all by divine grace, overflowing from His Holy Spirit, poured out to satisfy those who hear them.

45.1.2.en: 2- Christ is the Savior of those who believe in Him throughout the generations, and forever He gives them joy in the Kingdom through His salvation, with blessings that cannot be expressed. Likewise the Apostles, the priests and the servants speak the words of Christ throughout the generations and God blesses them, so that they become a blessing to all who hear them, and He glorifies them with Himself in the Kingdom forever.

45.1.3.en: 3- The grace poured into the lips of Christ gave us and prepared for us the enjoyment of Him in:

45.1.4.en: a- Partaking of the Holy Sacraments.

45.1.5.en: b- Delighting in His word, which gives us spiritual illumination, so that we are satisfied by it all our days.

45.2.0.en: 3- Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty.

45.2.1.en: 1- The sword is the word of God and the thigh is the body, so the girding on of the sword and its being joined to the thigh point to the Incarnation of the Second Hypostasis, the Word. This union between divinity and humanity surpasses the human mind, and none can accomplish it but God the Mighty One. The Incarnation revealed glory and majesty, that is, the greatness and light of the Father. For no one has seen God at any time, but the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared Him (Jn 1:2).

45.2.2.en: 2- The sword is also a type of the Cross. By Christ's being fastened to the Cross He proclaimed His might and authority, for by His death He bound Satan and trampled down death, and the greatness of God appeared in His crucifixion. He freed the captives in Hades, Adam and his children, and raised them up to Paradise, since He paid the debt that was upon them. Thus in the weakness of the Cross Christ proclaimed His might and the perfection of His power by delivering His children, and He showed this to us in His Resurrection.

45.3.0.en: 4- And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.

45.3.1.en: 1- David asks Christ to storm the kingdom of Satan in order to free His children from the dominion of evil, and to ride upon the Cross, He who is the righteous, the truth and the meek, and by the power of His right hand to make Satan afraid and bind him.

45.3.2.en: 2- Christ the King, entering the battle, does not fight like other kings to exalt Himself, but is perfect in His greatness, so He storms in to reign over the hearts of His children ("ride"), and removes from them the dominion and reign of Satan, that they may walk in truth, righteousness and humility like Him by the power of His Holy Spirit. Indeed, He gives them by His right hand to make the demons afraid and to trample all the power of the enemy, as He trampled Satan by His Cross.

45.4.0.en: 5- Thine arrows are sharp in the heart of the king's enemies; whereby the people fall under thee.

45.4.2.en: 1- The sharp arrows, that is, the keen, strong, piercing ones that destroy whomever they strike, are a type of the Cross, which bound the demons, who are the enemies of the King. The arrows are also the preaching of Christ by the hands of the Apostles, and then of the priests and servants throughout the generations. They may also be a type of the Romans who destroyed Jerusalem in AD 70 and destroyed the enemies of the King, that is, the enemies of Christ, who are the Jews.

45.4.3.en: 2- The peoples who fell under the hand of Christ are the demons whom Christ bound by His Cross, or they are the Gentiles and the Jews who believed in Christ and fell under His hand, that is, His authority, believing in His salvation.

45.5.0.en: 6- Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.

45.5.1.en: 1- The writer here speaks directly about Christ, saying to Him, "Thy throne, O God," is lasting for ever and ever, and no king can reign forever except Christ. The throne of God is the Cross on which He was crucified, that He might reign over the hearts of His children forever. Therefore the Church chants this psalm in a distinctive long melody on Great Friday and on the Tuesday of Holy Week.

45.5.2.en: 2- The sceptre of Christ's kingdom is the Cross, and it is a right sceptre because He is the only King who does not err. He is upright in His tenderness and in His discipline, and with His sceptre He guides us to the upright life.

45.6.0.en: 7- Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

45.6.1.en: 1- Because Christ alone is without sin, and is the righteous and holy One who hates evil, He alone was able to redeem mankind. So He was anointed with the Holy Spirit in the River Jordan, and the Holy Spirit appeared in the form of a dove. Christ did not need this anointing for Himself, but the Spirit came upon Him, that is, the coming of the Holy Spirit upon His head was shown to us, so that He might accomplish our redemption; it is a descent on our behalf. By this Christ takes His steps toward the joy set before Him, which is the accomplishment of our salvation on the Cross. Therefore the verse says that the anointing was with the oil of gladness, and to express the work of the Holy Spirit in all the children of God who will believe in Christ the Redeemer, as the Holy Spirit fills them with joy.

45.6.2.en: 2- The coming of the Holy Spirit upon Christ was a complete, hypostatic indwelling, and He appeared in the form of a dove. But the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles and the believers was in the form of divided tongues of fire, that is, a partial indwelling, according to their ability to bear it, so that He works in them and through them in service.

45.7.0.en: 8- All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.

45.7.1.en: Myrrh: a gummy liquid extracted from one of the trees abundant in the West, with a fragrant smell. The Magi presented it to Christ.

45.7.2.en: Aloes: sometimes called balm, a gummy liquid that flows from one of the trees abundant in Palestine, with a sweet smell. It was used as a perfume and in the burial of the dead.

45.7.3.en: Cassia: bark taken from one of the trees resembling the cinnamon tree, with the taste and smell of cinnamon. Ivory: the tusk of the elephant, with which palaces are adorned because it is costly.

45.7.4.en: 1- This verse speaks to us about Christ, whose garments, that is, His body, were perfumed with the fragrances of myrrh, aloes and cassia, because He bore sufferings for our sake, which are what myrrh signifies. Likewise He founded His churches, the palaces adorned with ivory, by His death on the Cross, because the tusks of ivory are not taken from the elephant except after its death.

45.7.5.en: 2- The garments of Christ are His churches and His children who cling to His body. These believers in Him are perfumed with many fragrances, which are their virtues, which they acquire when they carry the Cross and bear sufferings like Him. These sufferings are signified by myrrh, and the perfumes, that is, the virtues, are the sweet fragrances of myrrh, aloes and cassia. The palaces of ivory, as we mentioned, are the churches adorned with white ivory, which signifies splendor and glory. And the souls of the believers who are in the churches, by their praise of God, make Him glad and rejoice Him; therefore it says, "whereby they have made thee glad." The fragrances mentioned above are different, but all are beautiful; likewise the virtues and the fruits of the Spirit are different, but they adorn the souls of the believers.

45.8.0.en: 9- Kings' daughters were among thy honourable women: upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.

45.8.1.en: Honourable women: the women who are near, beloved and honored.

45.8.2.en: Ophir: a region in the south-east of the Arabian Peninsula, today's Yemen, distinguished by mines of the purest kinds of gold.

45.8.3.en: 1- The kings' daughters are the daughters of the great ones of the world, or the souls of the rich and those of high position, whose positions and wealth did not keep them from believing in Christ, so they became believers, drawn near to God, and among the honourable women, who are all the souls of those who believe in Christ, whether rich or poor, from the Jews or the Gentiles; for the love of Christ and His redemption will draw the souls of believers from the whole world in all its classes.

45.8.4.en: 2- The queen is the Church, or the Virgin, or the human soul that believes in Christ. Christ the King has set her at His right hand. The right hand signifies power and blessing, that is, Christ gave her grace and power more than all mankind, because she was adorned with the pure gold of Ophir, which signifies heaven, spirituality and lofty virtues.

45.8.5.en: 3- The gold of Ophir signifies the precious price that Christ paid to purchase His Church, that is, His blood shed on the Cross, the most precious thing in the world, which He offered out of love for His bride the Church; therefore the Church loves Him very much for giving His life for her.

45.8.6.en: If Christ calls you to draw near to Him to give you many blessings, and even gives you the love of a bridegroom for his bride and adorns you with every virtue, do not be lazy, but hasten to Him eagerly, and seize every opportunity to be with Him, so that you may enjoy His fellowship.

45.9.s.en: (2) The queen, the bride, and her glory

45.9.0.en: 10- Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father's house;

45.9.1.en: 1- God calls to the Church, or the Virgin, or every believing soul and says to her, "daughter," for He is the Father who cares for her, and He is Christ who redeemed her. David also calls to the Virgin who would come from his seed, that she may hear his spiritual guidance.

45.9.2.en: 2- God asks four important actions of every soul that believes in Him, which are:

45.9.3.en: a- "Hearken": that she hear Him attentively so as to obey His commandments.

45.9.4.en: b- "Consider": that she look at His beauty and contemplate it, so that as Christ lived, the believing soul imitates Him.

45.9.5.en: c- "Incline thine ear": that she be humble and incline her head toward the ground, as Christ carried His Cross and bowed His head to the ground for her sake, and as He washed the feet of His disciples.

45.9.6.en: d- "Forget thine own people": that is, that she leave behind all her old life in evil and all material attachments, so as to empty her heart for the love of God, and He becomes her Father who cares for her, and she submits to Him with all her heart, as Abraham left his family and his kindred and went out into the wilderness to live with God (Gen 12:1, 4), and as Ruth left her family and went with her mother-in-law to the land of Israel to worship God with His people (Ruth 1:16), and as the Apostles left everything and followed Christ (Mk 10:28).

45.10.0.en: 11- So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.

45.10.1.en: 1- When the Church, or the human soul, leaves her old life full of evil, that is, repents and believes in God, she becomes beautiful, because God forgives her and she becomes pure. And the wonder is that Christ the King desires her for her beauty which He Himself gave her, for she acquired her beauty from His beauty.

45.10.2.en: 2- On the other hand, Christ is the Creator of this soul, so He is her Lord and Master, and she is a queen and does not belong to anyone else. Therefore the soul submits to Him, responds to His love, and so she also desires Him, rejoices in her life with Him and praises Him.

45.11.0.en: 12- And the daughter of Tyre shall be there with a gift; even the rich among the people shall intreat thy favour.

45.11.1.en: 1- Tyre was the greatest commercial center in the world, and it was near the land of the Jews, lying to its north on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. It was rich, but unfortunately it was immersed in corruption and idolatry. The daughter of Tyre means the souls that believed in Christ, left behind their wealth and their evils, and drew near to the Church seeking her favor.

45.11.2.en: 2- The drawing near of the daughters of Tyre, that is, its people, is a type of all the Gentile peoples who believed in Christ and offered Him their gift, which is faith and repentance. By this they pleased the Church, and she received them into her membership. On this pattern the Magi went and came to Christ, being among the great and the rich of the world, and offered Him gifts.

45.12.0.en: 13- The king's daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold.

45.12.1.en: Her chamber: the inner room of the bride.

45.12.2.en: 1- He describes the bride, that is, the Church, or the believing soul, as having all her glory within, as the glory of the Tabernacle was within it, where the golden Ark of the Covenant, the altar, the lampstand and the golden table of the showbread were. As for the outside, it was skins of badgers, with no appearance, just as Christ Himself had no form nor comeliness (Isa 53:2), yet He is God the Savior of the world. Likewise the soul that believes in Christ has her beauty in her inner virtues, and does not seek to speak of them lest she fall into pride, and she lives a hidden life, that God may glorify her with glories that cannot be expressed in heaven, and she enjoys a hidden, secret relationship with Christ through the Holy Sacraments. Her outward appearance seems to be suffering, stripped and despised, but within her is joy and satisfaction in her heavenly Bridegroom.

45.12.3.en: 2- The garments of the bride are woven with gold, as in the Tabernacle and the Temple of Solomon.

45.12.4.en: Gold signifies heaven, so the bride lives a heavenly life and is adorned with virtues; indeed she is the temple of the Holy Spirit, and her heart is fixed on heaven, where her Bridegroom is, who is concerned to look upon her heart and her inner beauty.

45.13.0.en: 14- She shall be brought unto the king in raiment of needlework: the virgins her companions that follow her shall be brought unto thee.

45.13.1.en: 1- The king's daughter, that is, the souls that enter into the faith and live with Christ, wears embroidered garments, that is, her life is adorned with virtues. She does not come forward to Christ the King empty-handed, but with virtues and good works, because she loves Him and her heart is attached to Him, and she expresses her love through these works. Love is expressed through spiritual striving, as it says, "shall be brought."

45.13.2.en: 2- And behind the souls that began with Christ in faith, that is, behind the first Church that was founded on the disciples and the Apostles and those who believed on the day of Pentecost, many came forward to the faith; they believed through the hands of the Apostles and the preachers and came forward to Christ, so the Church expanded and spread throughout the whole world. Did the Apostles believe that all these priests and servants would come after them throughout the generations?! And likewise St. Stephen, the first martyr: did he imagine the multitudes of martyrs who would come after him until today?! And St. Anthony, the father of monks: did he imagine that all these monks in the world would come after him?!

45.13.3.en: All these souls are virgins, meaning spiritual virginity, that is, hearts consecrated to God, with no place for evil within them. They reject idolatry and keep away from all evil by repentance.

45.14.0.en: 15- With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king's palace.

45.14.1.en: 1- The souls that believed in Christ rejoiced and entered to Christ the King in His Church, to live a life of constant joy through their relationship with Christ the King, and through the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace. These souls came forward of their own free will, and with joy, to live with Christ, enjoy His love, and express their joy by constant praise of Him.

45.14.2.en: 2- The souls of the believers enter into the palace of the King, that is, they are near Him to enjoy His love. And as they are faithful in their love for Him inside the earthly palace of the King, inside the Church, they become worthy of the heavenly palace, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

45.15.0.en: 16- Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.

45.15.1.en: The king's daughter does not apply to the Jewish nation, for it did not have children in place of its fathers who became princes in all the earth. It applies only to the Church, which in place of her fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and all the fathers and prophets, has sons who are princes over the whole earth, namely the bishops and priests, who led the Church and the whole world in the way of life with Christ.

45.16.0.en: 17- I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever.

45.16.1.en: 1- David ends the psalm with a covenant which God offers, namely that he will remember God and glorify Him and live with Him all the days of his life, indeed from generation to generation. By this he means that his seed of believing Jews will continue to remember the name of God, and then whoever of them believes in Christ will continue to praise His holy name through the days. When the believer remembers the name of God he enjoys fellowship with Him and lives in His fear, so he keeps away from every sin, and then becomes an example to those around him, as they see the power of God in him and believe in his God. And the psalms that David wrote are chanted by the believers from generation to generation, that is, they pray and praise with them throughout the ages until today.

45.16.2.en: 2- In this verse David declares a prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles by saying, "shall the people praise thee," that is, the Gentiles who will believe in Christ in the whole world and remember His name like David, so they enjoy all the spiritual blessings, and continue to remember the name of God throughout the generations on earth, and then extend in praising the name of God forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

45.16.3.en: Delight in remembering the name of God many times every day, that your mind, and then your heart, may be lifted up to Him; this will give you peace, and then God will reveal His secrets to you and give you joy in His fellowship, and you will live in joy forever.

45.16.4.en: The Lord of hosts our refuge. To the chief musician, for the sons of Korah, upon Alamoth, a song: "God is our refuge and strength ... v. 1"

45.16.6.en: 1- Its writer: the sons of Korah, that is, one of the descendants of Korah, who were Levite singers.

45.16.8.en: a- A prophecy about the victory of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, over three peoples who attacked him, the children of Ammon, Moab and Edom (2 Chr 20:20-24).

45.16.9.en: b- A prophecy about the victory of King Hezekiah over the army of Sennacherib by the angel of the Lord (2 Kgs 19:35).

45.16.10.en: c- A prophecy about the victory of Christ by the Cross over Satan, his binding, and the occurrence of an earthquake, which happened at the ninth hour on Great Friday (Mt 27:51).

45.16.11.en: 3- The title of this psalm is written "upon Alamoth"; the Alamoth is a high vocal range similar to what is now the soprano range, in which the singers sang in the days of David (1 Chr 15:20).

45.16.12.en: 4- In the title it also says of this psalm that it is a "song," that is, a hymn of praise said in the Temple.

45.16.13.en: 5- This psalm is connected with the psalm before it. In the forty-fifth psalm we see the union of the bride with her Bridegroom and His glorifying her, that is, Christ's glorifying the Church. In this psalm he makes clear that the Church will meet tribulations, but God supports her, establishes her and gives her victory.

45.16.14.en: 6- This psalm is a song of praise, or a hymn of thanksgiving, and the two following psalms, 47 and 48, agree with it in this purpose.

45.16.15.en: 7- Some churches pray this psalm on the Feast of the Theophany (Epiphany), on the feast of the wedding at Cana of Galilee, and at the consecration of new churches.

45.16.16.en: 8- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Third Hour, which reminds us of the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the Church, because it speaks to us about the power of the Holy Spirit who supports, establishes and gives victory to the Church.
